review_candidates.description: We are hiring one senior Business Development Manager to own international new business. This is a hunting role, not an account-servicing role. ### What you will do - Build and work an outbound pipeline of print-on-demand platforms, screen printers, embroidery contractors, promotional product distributors and apparel brands across the US, Canada, UK and the EU — through email, LinkedIn, calls, industry directories and trade associations. - Qualify fast and honestly: how many designs a month, what turnaround they need, what they pay today, and what is going wrong with their current vendor. - Convert interest into trial orders — coordinate sample digitizing with the production team, present the sew-out, and handle the technical objections that follow. - Negotiate and close: pricing per design and per stitch-count slab, turnaround SLAs, volume commitments, payment terms, NDAs and vendor-onboarding paperwork. - Represent Cre8iveSkill at international trade shows (ISS, PRINTING United, Impressions Expo, FESPA, Texprocess and similar) — pre-show outreach, booth conversations, and follow-up that run all the way to a closed account. - Own the first 60–90 days of every new account: brief production properly, watch the early batches, and fix problems before the client has to escalate. - Keep the CRM real — every account, contact, stage, next action and expected value — with a weekly pipeline and revenue forecast to management. - Bring the market back to us: competitor pricing, what POD platforms are asking for, which techniques are gaining traction. - Work with marketing and design on outbound collateral, case studies, pricing decks, and trade-show material. - Manage time zones sensibly — a meaningful share of client conversation happens in US and European business hours. ### What we are looking for - 6–10 years in B2B business development or international sales, with a demonstrable record of closing accounts you sourced yourself. - Industry background in one of two worlds: an IT / IT services / software services company selling to overseas clients, **or** the fashion, apparel, textile, garment, or embroidery industry. - Real international exposure — you have sold to, negotiated with, or managed clients in the US and/or Europe, and you understand how those buyers evaluate an offshore vendor: on reliability, communication, and quality consistency, not only on price. - Excellent spoken and written English, and confidence on video calls with US and European decision-makers. - Commercial instinct — you can build a quote, defend a price, spot a bad-fit deal and walk away from it. - Comfortable owning a weekly number and keeping a CRM management system that can be relied on. - Based in Nagpur or willing to relocate. This will move your application forward significantly. - Working knowledge of German, French, or Spanish, even at a conversational level. - Exposure to print-on-demand, decorated apparel, promotional products, or custom merchandise. - Familiarity with embroidery and digitizing vocabulary — stitch count, underlay, pull compensation, DST/EMB file formats — or a genuine willingness to learn it within 60 days. - Trade show and exhibition experience, including booth-level selling. - Experience selling a production or delivery service governed by turnaround SLAs. ### What success looks like in year one - A qualified, accurately forecast international pipeline that management can plan capacity against. - A defined number of new logos closed and moved past their first repeat order — the target is agreed with you in your first month. - At least two international trade shows worked end to end, with measurable closed business traceable to each. - A repeatable outbound playbook — messaging, pricing structure, objection handling — documented well enough that the next hire can run it. ### What we offer - Competitive fixed salary plus an uncapped performance-linked incentive on business you bring in. - Fully sponsored international travel to trade shows and client markets. - Direct working access to the founders — short decision chains, no layers to sell through internally. - A production capability that lets you sell things competitors physically cannot deliver. - The first BD hire of a growing international team, with a clear path to building and leading it.

As a Level 2 Support Analyst at Basis Technologies, you sit at the technical heart of the customer experience. Product depth, not project breadth. If you have come from a consultancy or service integrator (SI) background, you will know what it feels like to move on before you fully understand what you built. That visibility creates real progression opportunities for people who want them. No travel. Stable. Ownership. Many people in SAP consulting reach a point where the project rotation and travel stop being a feature and start being a cost. This role offers the technical challenge without that trade-off. You get autonomy, direct customer impact, and the stability of a growing product company. The Skills You Build Here Are Rare. Deep knowledge of SAP transport management, ABAP debugging, and change management processes in a product context — rather than implementation context — is a profile that is hard to find and well-compensated across the market. Aside from the benefits of role evolution, tangible individual impact, and personal growth that you would expect working in a global scale-up environment, at Basis Technologies we take looking out for our employees seriously. Benefits include: Competitive salary Global Flexibility – work abroad for up to one month per year Enhanced Parental Leave Paid Volunteer Day Employee Referral Bonus Learning and Development Budget – each employee receives support to continue growing professionally Mental Health First Aiders Programme Who We Are Basis Technologies has been officially named one of the UK's Best Workplaces™ by Great Place to Work® for three consecutive years. We are a team of 130+ people operating across the UK, US, and Budapest — collaborative, fast-moving, and genuinely invested in the people who join us.
